brief: Pick one real task in your own field where you are considering AI. The rest of the lab builds a design for it, so choose something you can describe in detail.
do: Describe the task in three sentences: who asks, what the input is, what a good result looks like and who checks it.
List the three shapes for your task and say, in a sentence each, how it would work.
Score the four signals (path unknown, result checkable, wrong step cheap to undo, cost acceptable) as yes, partly or no, with a reason for each.
Write the decision record: choice, reasons, rejected options and the event that would make you revisit it.
done: Task description: Input, good result and who checks it are all stated
Signals: All four scored with a reason each
Options: Three shapes compared with the signals
Decision record: Choice, reasons, rejected options and a revisit event
Evidence: The task description, the signal scores with reasons, and the five-line decision record.
experienced: Apply it to an agent system you run or plan to run, with real tools, real limits, real owners and real dates.

tips: Set a timer for the step and write a rough first version before you polish. A rough answer is easier to improve than a blank page.
Write for the next person who has to act on this, not for a marker. Use plain words and name things.
Stuck on your own system? Use the sample case in the worked example for this step, then come back to yours.
Prefer numbers, names and dates to adjectives. If you do not know a number, write your best estimate and label it as an estimate.
Save often. Your work stays in this browser only, so download your file at the end of every session.
example:
**Task.** Customers of the Doubles-to-Go app report a missing item or a late order. A vendor reads the report, checks the order and replies, and may refund. Good result: the right reply and the right refund within 15 minutes, checked by the vendor.

**Shapes.** (A) Workflow: classify, then send a template. (B) Assistant: draft a reply and a refund suggestion for the vendor to approve. (C) Agent: investigate and refund by itself.

**Signals.** Path unknown: partly (most cases follow three patterns). Result checkable: yes (order record and payment record). Wrong step cheap to undo: no (a refund cannot be recalled easily). Cost acceptable: partly (about TT$0.40 a case against vendor time).

**Decision.** Choose B. Reasons: refunds are not cheap to undo and checks exist but are slow. Rejected: A (cannot handle variation), C (too risky now). **Revisit when** vendor-approved drafts reach the agreed accuracy for 60 days.
